system_overview: A high-level specification of a resource allocator managing a finite set of resources shared among a set of client processes. Clients request sets of resources, the allocator grants available resources (possibly partially), and clients return resources after use. The specification is deliberately abstract, omitting implementation details such as communication mechanisms and scheduling strategies.
actors_and_components: Two kinds of actors: client processes and the resource allocator. Clients issue resource requests, receive allocations, and return resources. The allocator tracks outstanding requests and granted allocations, ensuring exclusive access to resources.
state_variables: Two mappings from clients to sets of resources: one tracking each client's outstanding (unsatisfied) resource requests, and one tracking the resources currently allocated to each client. A derived constant computes the set of currently available (unallocated) resources.
initial_state: No resources have been requested or allocated. Every client has an empty set of outstanding requests and an empty set of allocated resources.
actions: Three actions exist. (1) A client issues a request for a non-empty set of resources, but only if it has no pending requests and holds no resources. (2) The allocator grants a non-empty subset of available resources that the client has requested; partial fulfillment is allowed. (3) A client returns a non-empty subset of the resources it currently holds, even before its full request has been satisfied.
safety_properties: Resource mutual exclusion: no resource is ever allocated to two different clients simultaneously. A type correctness invariant ensures outstanding requests and allocations are functions from clients to subsets of resources.
liveness_properties: Three liveness properties are specified. (1) Clients will eventually return all resources once their requests are fully satisfied (weak fairness on the return action). (2) Every requested resource will eventually be allocated to the requesting client (strong fairness on allocation). (3) Each client's set of outstanding requests is infinitely often empty, meaning every request is eventually fully satisfied.
model_bounds: For model checking, the specification uses 3 clients and 2 resources as symbolic constants. Symmetry reduction over permutations of clients and resources is defined but noted as incompatible with liveness checking.
additional_assumptions: The set of resources is assumed to be finite. The set of clients need not be finite since only finitely many will have issued requests at any point. A client cannot extend a pending request once it has been issued. Two alternative system specifications are provided with different fairness conditions: the original requires clients to always eventually return held resources, while a weaker variant only requires returns after the full request is satisfied. The weaker variant does not guarantee all liveness properties.
